speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and a headache. To help narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (caused by Group A Streptococcus). The classic presentation of fever, headache, rhinorrhea followed by a pruritic rash spreading from the trunk to extremities, specifically with a facial rash that spares the perioral area, is highly characteristic of scarlet fever.
